_note: The code words of an Arduino sketch (issue #143), in ASD-STE100. keys: the words or signs in the code that show this explanation (lib/sketch/words.ts). void shows the explanation of the function after it. word: the name that the learner sees. level: the level of the project that teaches the word; after the learner passes it, the word shows with the terms on the dashboard. text: what the word does. example: one line of code. does: what the example does, as the end of a sentence that starts with the example. Each sentence has 20 words or fewer.

words.text: The setup function. Its code runs one time, when the Uno starts. Put pinMode here.
words.does: makes pin 13 an output, one time at the start.

words.text: The loop function. Its code runs again and again, after setup(). After the last line, it starts again at the top.
words.does: waits 500 ms, again and again.

words.text: Makes a variable with a value that cannot change. Use it for a pin number, so the name tells the job of the pin.
words.does: gives pin 13 the name ledPin.

words.text: Makes a variable: a name that keeps a whole number. You can change the number later with =.
words.does: keeps the value of pin 2 in the variable state.

words.text: Puts a value into a variable. It does not compare two values. To compare, use ==.
words.does: puts LOW into the variable state.

words.text: Tells the Uno how a pin works: OUTPUT, INPUT or INPUT_PULLUP. Put it in setup().
words.does: makes pin 13 an output, so it can give power to an LED.

words.text: Gives power to a pin (HIGH) or stops it (LOW). The pin must be an OUTPUT.
words.does: turns on the LED on pin 13.

words.text: Reads a pin. It gives HIGH when the pin has 5 V, and LOW when the pin touches ground.
words.does: reads the button on pin 2.

words.text: Stops the sketch for a time, in milliseconds (ms). 1000 ms is 1 second.
words.does: waits half a second.

words.text: Runs the code in its { } only when the test in its ( ) is true.
words.does: turns on the LED when the button is pressed.

words.text: Comes after the { } of an if. Its code runs only when the test of the if is false.
words.does: turns off the LED when the test of the if is false.

words.text: Compares two values. The test is true when the two values are the same.
words.does: is true when pin 2 reads LOW.

words.text: Compares two values. The test is true when the two values are different.
words.does: is true when pin 2 does not read LOW.

words.text: Changes a test that is true to false, and a test that is false to true.
words.does: turns on the LED when pin 2 reads LOW.

words.text: The value for power on: 5 V on the Uno. With digitalWrite, HIGH turns an LED on.
words.does: gives 5 V to pin 13.

words.text: The value for power off: 0 V, the same as ground. With digitalWrite, LOW turns an LED off.
words.does: gives 0 V to pin 13.

words.text: A mode for pinMode. The Uno controls the pin, for example to turn an LED on and off.
words.does: lets pin 13 give power.

words.text: A mode for pinMode. The Uno reads the pin. With no resistor, the pin floats and can read a wrong value.
words.does: lets the Uno read pin 2.

words.text: A mode for pinMode. The Uno reads the pin, and a resistor inside the Uno joins the pin to 5 V.
words.does: makes pin 2 read HIGH, and LOW only while you press its button.

words.text: The pin of the small LED marked L on the Uno. On the Uno, it is pin 13.
words.does: makes pin 13 an output.

words.text: Ends each line of code, as a full stop ends a sentence. Without it, the Uno does not know where the line stops.
words.does: is one full line of code.

words.text: Hold a group of lines together. Each { needs a } to close it.
words.does: puts delay(10); inside loop().

words.text: A note for people. The Uno does not run it. A // note stops at the end of the line. A /* */ note can have many lines.
words.does: runs only delay(500);.
